headline: Blue shark tags reveal a Celtic Sea nursery nobody had mapped
standfirst: Sixty tags deployed over two summers show juveniles holding in one patch of water for months at a time.

image.alt: A blue shark alongside a research vessel before release

body.text: Blue sharks were assumed to be more or less constantly on the move. The tag data says otherwise, at least for animals in their first two years: juveniles are holding station in a roughly 900 square kilometre area for up to five months.
The area sits partly inside an existing protected zone and partly outside it, which is the sort of finding that makes for a difficult year of meetings.
